title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-notes-riley
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the smart-routing / fallback / regional-failover incident on 2024-10-03 -> 2024-10-04. Keep notes of commands I ran, error snippets, tentative hypotheses, and next actions. This is messy by design.

TL;DR (user-facing summary for postmortem):
- Around 2024-10-03 18:12 UTC we saw a spike in 502/504 errors from hosted-api in eu-west-1 followed shortly by cross-region fallbacks to us-west-2. Fallback policy routed traffic to a model variant that was missing a KV-cache optimization, resulting in increased latency and subsequent circuit-breaker trips. Some clients saw degraded responses or timeouts for ~45 minutes.

Impact:
- 1.2% of API requests failed with 502/504s during window.
- Latency for fallback routed requests increased from median 120ms -> 900ms.
- Some customers on Dedicated experienced tail latency spikes when routing through fallback.

Timeline (rough):
- 18:08 UTC: First SLO alert (error rate threshold) for eu-west-1 route.
- 18:11:30 UTC: Smart-routing controller started triggering fallback policy for route "hosted-prod-chat-eu".
- 18:12-18:45 UTC: Multiple fallbacks to us-west-2 and global-pool; 502/504s and timeouts spike.
- 18:47 UTC: Manual mitigations (rollback recent routing-policy change + increase circuit-breaker thresholds) began.
- 19:05 UTC: Error rate returned to baseline.

Commands run (notes + outputs redacted where sensitive):
- curl to repro with request id header
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-Id: riley-debug-001" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1", "input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat  
  -> sometimes returned 502 Bad Gateway, sometimes 200 slow (~900ms)

- Check smart-routing-controller logs (k8s, eu-west-1 cluster):
  kubectl --context=eu-west-1 get pods -n redwood-routing
  kubectl --context=eu-west-1 logs deploy/smart-routing-controller -n redwood-routing --since=1h | grep "fallback" | tail -n 50
  -> saw repeated lines: "policy=regional-failover action=fallback target=us-west-2 reason=capacity_constraint model_variant=redwood-chat-1-q4"

- Check model availability in eu-west-1:
  curl -s https://model-catalog.internal/api/v1/models/redwood-chat-1/availability?region=eu-west-1 | jq .
  -> "available": false, "reason": "missing-kv-optimized-build"

- Pod logs for model-serving in us-west-2:
  kubectl --context=us-west-2 logs deploy/redwood-chat-1-servers -n redwood-serving --since=2h | grep "kv-cache" | tail -n 100
  -> warnings about unsupported kv-cache path for quantized builds; fallback path used leading to CPU fallback loops

- Check Redis KV cache keys (light sampling):
  redis-cli -h redis-cache.prod -n 1 keys "kv:hosted-prod-chat-eu:*" | wc -l
  -> some keys, but many misses when fallback started

- Circuit breaker events (service-mesh telemetry):
  curl -s https://mesh-telemetry/api/events?service=hosted-api&since=2024-10-03T18:00Z | jq '.[] | select(.type=="circuit_breaker")'
  -> multiple trips for instance ids inst-223, inst-227 between 18:12-18:40 UTC

- ELB/Target health checks (eu-west-1):
  aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:... --region eu-west-1
  -> several targets showed Unhealthy at 18:10-18:15 then returned Healthy after 18:50

Error snippets (copied):
- 502 response body (sample): "{"error":"upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers"}"
- Proxy log: "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream"
- Model server stderr: "ERROR: unsupported kv-cache path for q4_0 builds; falling back to naive cache. throughput drop expected."
- Mesh telemetry: "circuit_breaker: threshold exceeded, tripped for instance inst-227"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model build mismatch in eu-west-1: the curated model variant with kv-cache/kernel optimizations (q4 build) was not present in eu-west-1 due to a failed artifact promotion earlier that day -> smart-routing fell back to another region where a non-optimized variant run much slower and caused upstream timeouts and circuit breakers.
2) Routing-policy config bug: a recently merged change reduced the capacity_threshold for regional failover too aggressively; that caused earlier fallbacks than expected during normal transient load. (Evidence: policy change PR #4523 merged 17:45 UTC).
3) Health-check flapping on a subset of serving hosts in eu-west-1 (ELB marking Unhealthy) caused the controller to consider region degraded -> combined with policy change it triggered mass fallback.
4) Cache cold-start amplification: when fallback started, many requests missed KV cache and hit cold-model path causing CPU spikes and longer latencies, causing cascading failures.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses (done / TODO):
- [x] Confirm model artifacts: model-catalog API showed missing optimized build for region (strong support for hypothesis #1).
- [x] Check PR/Config change: reviewed PR#4523 (routing-policy change) -> lowered min_capacity_threshold from 5% -> 1% for canary routes. That would make fallback more sensitive (supports #2).
- [ ] Reproduce locally with small cluster using same model variants and policy to validate whether cold-cache -> high CPU -> circuit-breaker is plausible.
- [ ] Check artifact promotion logs (release-engineering) to find failure to upload eu-west-1 artifact.

Immediate mitigations we did / considered:
- Roll back PR#4523 temporarily to restore previous threshold (we did this at 18:47 UTC).
- Increase circuit-breaker threshold for hosted-api to avoid cascading trips (manual override via feature-flag until model artifacts restored).
- Force redeploy/promotion of optimized model build to eu-west-1 (in progress by release-eng).
- Add short-term rate-limit on cross-region fallback path to limit amplification (follow-up: implement quota per minute).

Follow-ups / Action items (owners):
- Release engineering: investigate failed artifact promotion to eu-west-1 and add guardrails (OWNER: Amara Patel)
- Serving-runtime: ensure model-catalog returns consistent availability; add alert if model missing in region (OWNER: Marcus O'Neill)
- Smart-routing: revert was temporary; add integration test for policy sensitivity; ensure canary thresholds have safety floor (OWNER: Ethan Park)
- SRE: review circuit-breaker defaults and add hysteresis for short flaps (OWNER: Riley Chen)
- Product/Console: add visibility for per-model-variant availability in Console so customers see fallback behaviors (OWNER: Zoe Martinez)

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- We should treat model-artifact promotion as a first-class dependency for routing decisions — if a model variant isn't fully promoted to a region, controller should ignore that variant entirely rather than rely on cross-region fallback.
- Consider marking model-variants with a "compatibility fingerprint" (kv-cache enabled flag) so the controller can prefer compatible variants only.
- Maybe the policy should have a cooldown window: don't re-evaluate fallback for X seconds after a mass fallback so we don't oscillate.

Unresolved questions:
- Why did ELB targets become Unhealthy briefly? (hardware vs autoscaler churn vs pod OOM?) Need kube events for nodes.
- Was there any overlap with Dedicated reserved capacity customers getting routed to fallback? (Telemetry looked limited but need customer-impact check)
- Does model-catalog reliability metric exist? If not, add one.

Raw artifacts / ids (for traceability):
- Alert id: alert-2024-10-03-18-08-euw1-01
- Example request ids (samples): riley-debug-001, riley-debug-002, riley-prod-394834
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4523
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/JIRA-1234

Next immediate steps (today):
1) Sync with release-eng on artifact promotion status (Amara) — check logs, re-upload if needed.
2) Add quick guard in smart-routing to treat missing optimized builds as incompatible (temp-hotfix by Ethan).
3) Add instrumentation to model-catalog endpoint to surface per-region build completion timestamps (Marcus).
4) Draft postmortem skeleton with timeline + impact numbers (I'll start the doc).

Misc scratch commands I left here for later:
- kubectl --context=eu-west-1 describe pod <pod-name> -n redwood-serving | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl --context=eu-west-1 get events -n redwood-serving --since=2h | grep -i oom
- aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name HealthyHostCount --namespace AWS/ApplicationELB --start-time 2024-10-03T18:00:00Z --end-time 2024-10-03T19:00:00Z --period 60 --statistics Average --region eu-west-1

If I remember more specifics I'll dump them here. Keep as single source of truth for immediate follow-ups before we move to the formal postmortem doc.

-- Riley
